We probably need to discuss naming on the SIG call. Some research ([doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1EKIeDgBGXQPGehUigIRLwAUpRGa7-1kXB736EaYuJ2M/edit?tab=t.6cg23pewoc2o)):

- **turn**: OpenAI Agents SDK (`max_turns`) and Anthropic tool runner use it for one model/tool loop iteration, the opposite of this PR. OpenAI Agents API (`/sessions/{id}/turns`) uses it the PR's way.
- **run**: OpenAI Agents SDK `Runner.run`, Microsoft Agent Framework `agent.run`, ADK `Runner.run_async`, Azure Foundry Agent Service `/threads/{id}/runs`, Google Agent Runtime `/api/run`.
- **invocation**: ADK `InvocationContext` (user message to final response), Microsoft Agent Framework agents-as-tools, AWS `InvokeAgent` / `InvokeAgentRuntime`, Azure Foundry hosted agents `/invocations`.


I think regardless of the noun, it needs to be qualified - turn / run / invocation are all vague. 

So options:

1. Don't qualify. `gen_ai.invocation | turn | run.duration` - not clear if it's related to agentic scenario
2. Qualify
    a. `agent_invocation | turn | run` - we're back to agent vs workflow vs wrapper terminology
    b. `agentic_invocation | turn | run` - more generic, a bit awkward

I'd like to check if we can entertain idea of `agent_invocation` | `invoke_agent` as the span type / metric name. We'd explain it covers workflow and any other wrapper. It'd still have the attribute to distinguish outer vs inner, operation name / span name are flexible and can be anything.

A nice side-effect is that we can keep existing agentic metrics.
